<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

Prefix sharing creates a scheduling trade-off: cache-cold requests with the same prefix can duplicate prefill work when admitted together, while delaying related requests too long risks losing reusable KV states to eviction. Repeated full-queue prefix matching and sorting can also offset the computation saved through reuse under high concurrency.

This PR adds `prefix-weave`, a scheduling policy that balances cached-prefix reuse and in-batch overlap while limiting repeated scheduling work, targeting repeated prompts and multi-turn conversations.

## Modifications

- Add `--schedule-policy prefix-weave` and document the policy in the server arguments and tuning guides.
- Implement adaptive tier ordering based on global-cache hit ratio and prefix overlap within the candidate batch, with cached-prefix length as the within-tier ordering key.
- Bound tier assignment with a token budget derived from the prefill configuration. Use the remaining request/token admission budget after chunked-prefill handling to skip reclassification when previously classified requests already cover the next admission.
- Record completed sequence lengths by routing key and use them to estimate prefix reuse for subsequent turns. Remove admitted requests from the retained classification set.
- Add unit coverage for tier precedence, classification reuse, and cross-turn prefix estimates; update affected test fixtures for the scheduler integration.

## Accuracy Tests

Environment:

- Hardware: `1 × NVIDIA H20-3e`
- Revision: `4080e3f59a`
- Tensor parallel size:  1
- Model: `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`
- Evaluator: `sgl-eval 0.1.2`; 200 GSM8K examples; 3 repeats per evaluation
- Server: memory fraction 0.80; seed 0
- Generation: temperature 0; top-p 0.95; max tokens 2048; concurrency 64
- Comparison: `fcfs` versus `prefix-weave`, with all other settings unchanged

Results:

| Policy           | Examples | Repeats | pass@1 | pass@1 std | majority@3 | no-answer | truncated | error |
| ---------------- | -------: | ------: | -----: | ---------: | ---------: | --------: | --------: | ----: |
| `fcfs`         |      200 |       3 | 82.00% |    1.00 pp |     82.50% |     5.00% |     1.33% | 0.00% |
| `prefix-weave` |      200 |       3 | 82.17% |    1.04 pp |     84.50% |     6.33% |     2.83% | 0.00% |

Pass@1 differs by +0.17 percentage points. No pass@1 regression was observed in this small sanity check; token-level equivalence was not evaluated.

<details>
<summary>Accuracy test commands</summary>

Run once with `--schedule-policy fcfs` and once with `--schedule-policy prefix-weave`.

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-type llm \
  --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --served-model-name meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 30000 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --schedule-policy fcfs \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --random-seed 0 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

```bash
sgl-eval run gsm8k \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \
  --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --num-examples 200 \
  --n-repeats 3 \
  --max-tokens 2048 \
  --num-threads 64
```

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Environment:

- Revision: `4080e3f59a`
- Model: `Meta-Llama-3.1-8B`
- Hardware: 4 × NVIDIA H20-3e; four concurrent TP=1 servers, one policy per GPU
- Policies: `fcfs`, `lpm`, `dfs-weight`, `prefix-weave`
- Server: memory fraction 0.85; max running requests 1,024; overlap scheduling disabled
- Client settings: same host as the servers; streaming; unlimited request rate; seed 1
- 500 warmup requests; cache flushed before each measured run; workloads run serially per server
- One run per workload and policy

Benchmarks used a custom client adapted from SGLang’s `bench_serving.py` to support repeated single-turn requests and sequential multi-turn session replay. All policies used the same client, source datasets, and generation settings.

Workloads:

| Workload                 | Shape                       | Completed requests |           Input tokens | Output tokens | Client concurrency limit |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------- | -----------------: | ---------------------: | ------------: | ------------------------ |
| MMLU-Pro 5-shot `aabb` | 4,096 prompts × 8 replicas |             32,768 |             36,969,736 |       196,608 | 4,096                    |
| MMLU-Pro 5-shot `abab` | 4,096 prompts × 8 replicas |             32,768 |             36,969,736 |       196,608 | unlimited                |
| BFCL multi-turn          | 5,106 sessions              |             17,029 | 94,413,028 (estimated) |     1,100,424 | unlimited                |

`aabb` groups eight replicas of each prompt together; `abab` interleaves replicas across prompts. Both use five-shot prompts and average 6 output tokens per request. BFCL submits each turn after the previous turn completes, including the generated conversation history.

Results (request throughput):

| Workload                 | FCFS req/s | LPM req/s | DFS-weight req/s | PrefixWeave req/s | Speedup vs FCFS | Speedup vs fastest existing policy |
| ------------------------ | ---------: | --------: | ---------------: | ----------------: | --------------: | ---------------------------------- |
| MMLU-Pro 5-shot `aabb` |     37.171 |    37.229 |           31.367 |           119.455 |          3.21× | 3.21× (lpm)                       |
| MMLU-Pro 5-shot `abab` |     12.803 |    12.841 |           38.919 |           100.898 |          7.88× | 2.59× (dfs-weight)                |
| BFCL multi-turn          |      2.981 |     3.189 |            4.203 |             6.971 |          2.34× | 1.66× (dfs-weight)                |

Speedup is baseline duration / PrefixWeave duration. LPM retains its default FCFS fallback for waiting queues above 128 requests.

Latency versus FCFS (seconds; BFCL values are per turn):

| Workload                 | Policy           | Mean TTFT |  P99 TTFT |  Mean E2E |   P99 E2E |
| ------------------------ | ---------------- | --------: | --------: | --------: | --------: |
| MMLU-Pro 5-shot `aabb` | `fcfs`         |    90.647 |   110.554 |   104.803 |   116.030 |
| MMLU-Pro 5-shot `aabb` | `prefix-weave` |    28.153 |   141.528 |    32.654 |   145.003 |
| MMLU-Pro 5-shot `abab` | `fcfs`         | 1,287.281 | 2,523.791 | 1,326.719 | 2,549.735 |
| MMLU-Pro 5-shot `abab` | `prefix-weave` |   177.742 |   317.634 |   181.535 |   320.884 |
| BFCL multi-turn          | `fcfs`         |   221.030 |   461.066 |   299.162 |   649.147 |
| BFCL multi-turn          | `prefix-weave` |   141.765 | 1,296.367 |   184.112 | 1,338.706 |

PrefixWeave improves throughput by **3.21×, 2.59×, and 1.66× over the fastest existing policy**, respectively. Mean TTFT and E2E latency improve versus FCFS, but P99 E2E increases by **25.0% on `aabb` and 106.2% on BFCL**. These single-run results cover saturated, prefix-heavy workloads with overlap disabled.

Scheduler profiling (server counters):

| Workload                 | FCFS cached-input ratio | PrefixWeave cached-input ratio | Scheduler time (s) | Scheduler time / duration |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------: | -----------------------------: | ------------------: | ------------------------: |
| MMLU-Pro 5-shot `aabb` |                  79.66% |                         95.49% |              19.033 |                     6.94% |
| MMLU-Pro 5-shot `abab` |                  37.86% |                         95.29% |              47.478 |                    14.62% |
| BFCL multi-turn          |                  60.16% |                         87.00% |             140.036 |                     5.73% |

Cached-input ratio is cached tokens / input tokens. Scheduler time measures the instrumented scheduling calculation path; the final column divides it by run duration. No profiler trace is included.

<details>
<summary>Speed test commands</summary>

Server example: repeat with `--schedule-policy fcfs`, `lpm`, `dfs-weight`, and `prefix-weave`, assigning a separate GPU (`--base-gpu-id`) and port to each concurrent server.

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B \
  --served-model-name Meta-Llama-3.1-8B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000 \
  --base-gpu-id 0 \
  --schedule-policy prefix-weave \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --max-running-requests 1024 \
  --disable-overlap-schedule \
  --enable-metrics \
  --enable-request-time-stats-logging \
  --trust-remote-code
```

The following example uses the custom client. `--rollout 8` creates eight replicas per prompt; `--rollout-order aabb` groups replicas of the same prompt together (`abab` interleaves them); `--max-concurrency 4096` limits concurrent requests to 4,096 (omit it for unlimited concurrency). Replace the dataset placeholders and match the port to the target server.

```bash
python /path/to/bench_serving.py \
  --backend sglang \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \
  --model Meta-Llama-3.1-8B \
  --tokenizer /path/to/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B \
  --dataset-name "<dataset-name>" \
  --dataset-path "/path/to/<dataset>.jsonl" \
  --num-prompts "<num-prompts>" \
  --rollout 8 --rollout-order aabb --max-concurrency 4096 \
  --request-rate inf --warmup-requests 500 --flush-cache --seed 1
```

</details>

## Checklist

- [X] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [X] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [X] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [X] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [X] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -80,3 +80,4 @@ Data parallelism is better for throughput. When there is enough GPU memory, alwa
 - Try other quantization (e.g. FP8 quantization with `--quantization fp8`)

+class TestPrefixWeave(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.policy = SchedulePolicy(
+            policy="prefix-weave",
+            tree_cache=RadixCache.create_simulated(),
+            enable_hierarchical_cache=True,
+            enable_priority_scheduling=False,
+            schedule_low_priority_values_first=False,
+            chunked_prefill_size=64,
+            max_prefill_tokens=128,
+        )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def make_req(rid, *, routing_key=None, prefix_len=0):
+        req = _make_req(
+            rid,
+            "",
+            list(range(10)),
+            routing_key=routing_key or f"key-{rid}",
+        )
+        req.prefix_len = prefix_len
+        return req
+
+    def test_tier_precedence_overrides_cached_prefix_length(self):
+        """A lower tier must not jump ahead because its prefix_len is larger.
+
+        PrefixWeave combines global-cache reuse with marginal in-batch overlap.
+        Reversing either comparison silently changes which requests are admitted
+        first, even though every request still receives a valid numeric score.
+        """
+        tier_1 = self.make_req("tier-1", prefix_len=1)
+        tier_2 = self.make_req("tier-2", prefix_len=9)
+        tier_3 = self.make_req("tier-3", prefix_len=8)
+        unclassified = self.make_req("unclassified", prefix_len=10)
+        queue = [unclassified, tier_3, tier_2, tier_1]
+
+        global_cached = {
+            "tier-1": 8,
+            "tier-2": 8,
+            "tier-3": 1,
+            "unclassified": 1,
+        }
+        batch_overlap = {
+            "tier-1": 0,
+            "tier-2": 9,
+            "tier-3": 0,
+            "unclassified": 2,
+        }
+
+        with (
+            patch(
+                "sglang.srt.managers.schedule_policy.match_kv_cache",
+                side_effect=lambda req, tree_cache, token_ids=None: SimpleNamespace(
+                    device_prefix_len=global_cached[req.rid]
+                ),
+            ),
+            patch.object(
+                self.policy,
+                "_match_batch_prefix_for_req",
+                side_effect=lambda req, token_ids=None: SimpleNamespace(
+                    device_prefix_len=batch_overlap[req.rid]
+                ),
+            ),
+            patch.object(self.policy, "_insert_inbatch_tree"),
+        ):
+            self.policy.calc_priority(queue, max_req_num=4, token_budget=128)
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [req.rid for req in queue],
+            ["tier-1", "tier-2", "tier-3", "unclassified"],
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(self.policy.classified_reqs, {"tier-1", "tier-2", "tier-3"})
+
+        self.policy.update_classified_reqs([tier_1, tier_3])
+        self.assertEqual(self.policy.classified_reqs, {"tier-2"})
+
+    def test_full_classification_budget_keeps_existing_order(self):
+        """Previously classified work filling the request budget is not reshuffled.
+
+        This preserves the admission decision across scheduler passes and keeps
+        the policy's calculation counter limited to actual classifications.
+        """
+        first = self.make_req("first")
+        second = self.make_req("second")
+        queue = [first, second]
+        self.policy.classified_reqs = {first.rid}
+
+        with patch(
+            "sglang.srt.managers.schedule_policy.match_kv_cache",
+            return_value=SimpleNamespace(device_prefix_len=0),
+        ):
+            self.policy.calc_priority(queue, max_req_num=1, token_budget=128)
+
+        self.assertEqual(queue, [first, second])
+        self.assertEqual(self.policy.classified_reqs, {first.rid})
+        self.assertEqual(self.policy.calc_count, 0)
+
+    def test_finished_routing_length_is_reused_for_next_turn(self):
+        """The latest completed length seeds the next turn's cache estimate.
+
+        The completion path and the next scheduling pass are separate call sites;
+        losing their routing-key handoff degrades multi-turn cache prioritization
+        without causing a request failure.
+        """
+        finished = self.make_req("finished", routing_key="conversation")
+        finished.output_ids.extend([10, 11])
+        self.policy.update_finished_reqs_info(finished)
+        finished.output_ids.append(12)
+        self.policy.update_finished_reqs_info(finished)
+
+        next_turn = self.make_req("next", routing_key="conversation")
+        with patch(
+            "sglang.srt.managers.schedule_policy.match_kv_cache"
+        ) as global_match:
+            calculated = self.policy._prefix_weave_phase0_presort(
+                [next_turn], max_req_num=1, max_token=128
+            )
+
+        self.assertTrue(calculated)
+        self.assertEqual(self.policy.finished_req_lengths["conversation"], 13)
+        self.assertEqual(self.policy.estimated_cached_tokens["conversation"], 13)
+        global_match.assert_not_called()
+
